analysis.title: O'Reilly Automotive Inc. (ORLY): Takeaways from virtual group meeting with CFO
key_insights: GS hosted a virtual group meeting with ORLY CFO Jeremy Fletcher and Leslie Skorick (Senior Director of Tax and Investor Relations). Topics: components of elevated 3Q SG&A, drivers of the higher FY26 SG&A per store outlook, motor oil gross margin headwind, and accelerating unit growth.

GS maintains Buy on ORLY. It expects ORLY to take share in the current environment and outperform peers, particularly in DIFM (do-it-for-me), and cites accelerating share repurchases alongside reinvestment in the business as aids to near-term and longer-term EPS growth.

3Q SG&A per store grew 4.8%, above expectations. Management attributed it to deploying incremental dollars into execution as the company outperformed on average ticket and traffic, plus wage rates up a little over 3% and higher fuel, employee medical, and claims/litigation costs.

FY26 SG&A per store growth expectation is now 4.5%-5.0% y/y. Management is comfortable with the higher floor because the costs tie to the competitive advantages behind share gains (team quality, training), and reaffirmed confidence in driving incremental profitability rate gains.

Petroleum-based categories, mainly motor oil, added about 1pp to ORLY's +7.2% 3Q comp but were a 0.4pp headwind to margin. Management calls it an industry-wide headwind, and some peers also said price increases did not hold gross margin rate.

ORLY raised prices enough to grow gross profit dollars in the motor oil category in 3Q. Management reaffirmed its pricing power. GS expects product margins to return to a normal range over time but sees the cost/price environment as a near-term headwind.

Tariff refunds from suppliers on ORLY's initial tariff obligations drove $39mn of direct pass-through in 3Q, a 76bps benefit to gross margin. Management expects an incremental benefit in 4Q as supplier negotiations continue.
Excluding the $39mn tariff refund benefit, 3Q EBIT grew close to 9%. Management reaffirmed confidence in sustained improvement and share gains.

Square footage is growing faster than store count because newer store formats are larger and the hub store strategy is producing larger hubs through renovation, expansion, and relocation. Management said not all added square footage shows up as a comp benefit.

Management sees room to consolidate the fragmented US DIFM market, expanding within existing markets and into new ones such as the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast. In mature markets like Texas, new stores perform well and impact on nearby existing stores normalizes quickly in almost every instance.

MEMA put underperformed maintenance at $102bn in 2025, up from $43bn in 2024, and ORLY kept gaining share. A few discretionary areas and larger-ticket jobs were under pressure in 3Q, while consumers prioritized maintenance on existing cars and hot weather categories were strong.

ORLY is Buy rated and on the US Conviction List. The 12-month price target is $104 against a $89.79 price (15.8% upside), based on relative P/E multiples of 120%/140%/150% for downside/base/upside cases.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy after the CFO meeting. ORLY is on the US Conviction List, with share gains in DIFM and accelerating buybacks supporting EPS growth. The 12-month target of $104 implies 15.8% upside from $89.79.

earnings_insights: ORLY 3Q (reported): comp +7.2%, with petroleum-based categories such as motor oil contributing about +1pp to comp and a 0.4pp headwind to margin.
ORLY 3Q (reported): SG&A per store +4.8% y/y, above expectations. FY26 SG&A per store guidance is 4.5%-5.0% y/y.
ORLY 3Q (reported): $39mn of tariff refund pass-through from suppliers, a 76bps benefit to gross margin. Management expects an incremental benefit in 4Q. EBIT grew close to 9% excluding the $39mn.

GS estimates (forecast): ORLY EPS $0.79 for 12/26E (4Q) and $0.78 for 3/27E, against $0.97 for 9/26 (3Q, shown in GS's quarterly table). FY EPS is $2.97 for 12/25, $3.33 for 12/26E, $3.72 for 12/27E, and $4.09 for 12/28E.
GS estimates (forecast): ORLY revenue is $19,309mn for 12/26E and $20,555mn for 12/27E, against $17,782mn for 12/25. EBIT is $3,819mn for 12/26E and $4,055mn for 12/27E.
risk_factors: Demand headwinds, particularly in discretionary categories, from broader macro pressure.
Elevated inflation in certain non-controllable expenses.
Higher distribution costs from supply chain headwinds and labor cost increases.
Operating margin risk as DIFM penetration increases and ORLY invests in recruiting and retaining talent.
Purchase deferral and other DIY demand headwinds.
Motor oil cost/price dynamics likely remain a near-term gross margin headwind.
